andriyash-scope-local-update-qmc-stoquas: Section I, p.1: the paper states it considers only QMC with local updates, and that these need a stoquastic Hamiltonian.
andriyash-definition-qmc-simulates-qa: Section I, p.2: the paper states its own criterion for QMC as a simulation of QA and which QMC variants it excludes, with its reason. Footnote [32] notes the T much smaller than 2g exception; the value says only what the authors state.
andriyash-setup-incoherent-regime: Section II A, pp.2-3: it states it focuses on incoherent tunneling and QMC escape at one point s*, small tunneling amplitude (s* near 1), and identical double-well minima.
andriyash-setup-temperature-regime: Section II A, p.3: it states the temperature regime (2g < T << dE) and that thermally assisted tunneling is beyond the scope.
andriyash-qmc-classical-mapping: Section III, p.3 states the D to D+1 mapping with the periodic imaginary-time dimension. Appendix A (Eqs. A1-A9, pp.9-10) derives it by the Trotter decomposition for a transverse-field Hamiltonian. It is derived in the paper, not only cited.
andriyash-boundary-partition-function: Section III A, pp.3-4: Eq. (9) gives Z for the two-level regime 2g << T << dE. Eqs. (11)-(14) give ZB/Z0 = beta^2 g^2, and Eq. (13) derives ZB to lowest order in Delta with the conditions stated. The all-orders extension is graded separately (LOW).
andriyash-two-paths-suppression-conditio: Section III B 2, p.6: the paper states the condition (20), the energy gap must offset the entropy difference, and that the gap must grow with size. It also states that when violated the four configurations may set the rate, giving Eq. (17) with no factor of 2. The value's 'disappears' is slightly firmer than the text's 'may'; the quotes carry the point.
andriyash-frustrated-ring-size-limit: Section IV B, p.7: the paper states that at very large N the inter-path loops may escape through entropy and reduce the factor of 1/2 unless J/epsilon grows with N.
andriyash-shamrock-numerics-setup: Section IV C, p.7 and Fig. 6 caption, p.8: continuous-time QMC from the all-up state, Delta=A=0.5, B=1, beta=20, J=6, epsilon=0.2, 5% support threshold, 1000 independent runs, all as the paper states.
andriyash-shamrock-entropy-limit: Section IV C, p.8: the paper states that inter-path loop entropy must be watched as the shamrock scales and that J/epsilon may need to grow linearly with N. This is a caveat on its own result; its true type is theoretical, not measured.
andriyash-limit-tunneling-physics-not-ca: Section V, p.8 (page image checked): the paper states the rate (1) leaves out resonant tunneling and polaron effects, which QMC does not capture, and that an extra sqrt(N) advantage is expected beyond Fig. 6. The sqrt(N) is confirmed on the page image. The extra advantage is the authors' expectation, stated as a caveat on what Fig. 6 shows.
arrieta-definition-explainable-ai: Section 2.2, p.6: the authors pose this definition of explainable AI and call it a first contribution of the overview.
arrieta-definition-explainability-audien: Section 2.2, p.6: the authors give the two audience-dependence ambiguities and rephrase the definition of explainability to include the audience.
arrieta-definition-interpretability-vs-e: Section 2.1, pp.4-5: the authors distinguish interpretability (passive, also called transparency) from explainability (active) in their own terminology clarification.
arrieta-definition-transparency-levels: Section 2.1, p.5: the survey's own transparency definition and the three-category split used in Section 3. It cites [5] for the categories, but the survey adopts them as its framework.
arrieta-definition-simulatability: Section 2.5.1, p.10: the survey's own definition of simulatability.
arrieta-definition-decomposability: Section 2.5.1, p.11: the survey's own definition of decomposability and its added constraint over algorithmic transparency.
arrieta-definition-algorithmic-transpare: Section 2.5.1, p.11: the survey's own definition of algorithmic transparency and its main constraint.
arrieta-transparency-levels-nested: Section 2.5.1, p.10: the survey states as part of its definition of the three levels that each class contains its predecessors.
arrieta-posthoc-categories: Section 2.5, p.10 and Section 2.5.2, p.11: the survey's own list of post-hoc technique categories and the order of its classification (intention, method, data type).
arrieta-scope-400-contributions: Section 1, p.3, contribution 3: the survey states it covers approximately 400 contributions in two taxonomies.
arrieta-definition-responsible-ai: Section 1, pp.3-4: the term 'Responsible AI' is defined at its first use, and contribution 5 states that fairness, accountability and privacy are included alongside explainability.
arrieta-scope-no-metric-design: Section 5.2, p.31: the survey states it does not tackle the design of a suite of explainability metrics.
arrieta-data-fusion-levels-definition: Section 6.3.1, p.41: 'we will distinguish among' data, model and knowledge level fusion, plus centralized and distributed categories. This is the categorization the paper adopts for its own use, taken from cited surveys [409-412].
arute-setup-sycamore-device: Main text, p.1: the paper states the 54-qubit Sycamore device, four-neighbor coupling, a largest simulation of a dozen qubits, and nearest-neighbor coupling only.
arute-setup-systems-simulated: Main text, pp.1-2: the paper states H6, H8, H10 and H12 chains and the diazene isomerization.
arute-setup-qubit-mapping: Main text, p.2: N qubits for 2N spin-orbitals under the equal spatial orbitals constraint, and 10 qubits for diazene after pre-processing.
arute-setup-basis-set: Appendix A, p.11: the one-body integrals are described in the STO-3G atomic basis.
arute-setup-benchmark-geometries: Appendix J, p.29: OpenFermion and Psi4 for the integrals, and the six separations 0.5 to 2.5 Angstrom.
arute-claim-hartree-fock-classically-sim: Main text, pp.2-3: the paper states the circuits are classically simulable in O(N^3) and the ansatz is efficient to simulate classically. This is a limit on what the experiment shows. The 'compelling experiment' part is the authors' stated argument.
arute-diazene-target-accuracy: Main text, pp.2 and 5: the paper states the 40 milliHartree target and that Hartree-Fock reverses the transition-state order, so it focuses on accuracy to the simulated model, not to the true chemistry.
arute-circuit-size-h12: Figure 1 caption, p.2: 72 iswap gates, 108 single-qubit Z rotations and 36 variational parameters, consistent with 36 Givens rotations.
arute-circuit-size-diazene: Figure 3 caption, p.4: 50 iswap gates and 80 Rz gates per basis rotation, as the caption states.
arute-1rdm-measurement-protocol: Main text, p.4: the protocol measures all N^2 1-RDM elements with N+1 circuits, 250,000 measurements each.
arute-error-mitigation-two-types: Main text, p.4: post-selection on particle number and pure-state projection.
arute-postselection-cost: Main text, p.4: two T gates and one iswap per qubit pair, and post-selection on the excitation number.
arute-purification-limit: Main text, p.4: the paper states McWeeny purification works only for Slater determinant wavefunctions. The mention of more general N-representability conditions [31] is context for that limit.
arute-optimizer-description: Main text, p.4: the paper's own optimizer, built on the Brillouin-condition proposal [34], with update-size regularization [35].
arute-optimizer-iterations: Figure 2 caption p.3 and Figure 3 caption p.4: 18 to 30 iterations for H6; 30 for diazene except two in-plane points at 60.
arute-fig2-setup-classical-angles: Figure 2 caption, p.3: the raw, post-selection and purification points use classically computed optimal angles.
arute-error-bars-method: Figure 2 caption p.3 and Appendix C 5, p.16: covariance estimate, Gaussian resampling, 1000 resamples, mean and standard deviation.
arute-table1-fidelity-setup: Table I caption, p.5: averaging over the six separations and the gate and readout error rates for the estimate column.
arute-fidelity-witness-limit: Main text and Table I caption, p.5: the paper states the witness is a lower bound that may be loose at small fidelity, in particular the raw H12 value.
arute-fidelity-witness-definition: Appendix D 1, p.17: the paper defines a fidelity witness as a strict lower bound observable and states its L^2 cost (adapted from [36]).
arute-device-drift-caveat: Appendix I 3, p.29: the paper states a caveat on its own data: performance varied across collection days (TLS diffusion), the H10 set was likely taken at a worse time than H12, and all results are shown without re-running. The cause is hedged ('likely'), but the caveat on comparability is the authors' own.
arute-geometry-diazene-reduction: Appendix J, pp.29-30: Psi4 constrained geometry optimizations, and the 10 qubit reduction by two SCF cycles with the bottom two levels integrated out.

theory_low.andriyash-boundary-partition-all-orders: Appendix C, pp.10-11: the all-orders claim is argued, not proved. Eq. (C5) is not evaluated ('seems to be out of reach'). The conclusion (C8) drops derivative terms under the assumption beta b b' << beta^2 a' b^2 at low temperature and b << a.
theory_low.andriyash-single-path-same-scaling: Section III B 1, p.5: the step ZB = Zbarrier and the rate proportional to Zbarrier/Z0 (Eq. 15) rest on a Kramers-type proportionality that the text only says it 'expects'. A perturbative heuristic, not a theorem.
theory_low.andriyash-two-paths-factor-two: Section III B 2, pp.5-6: a schematic argument from Figs. 2-3. The suppression of inter-path loops is assumed and holds only under condition (20), which the paper gives separately. Not a proof.
theory_low.andriyash-many-paths-scaling: Section III B 3, p.6: Npaths^2 against Npaths is a scaling argument extended from the two-path case, conditional on forbidden inter-path channels. Not a proof.
theory_low.andriyash-uniform-ferromagnet-no-advanta: Section IV A, p.6: an argument for one example (homotopy equivalence of the N! paths), with a claim of agreement with and generality over Isakov et al. [1]. The authors' claim, not a proved theorem.
theory_low.andriyash-frustrated-ring-two-paths: Section IV B, p.7: a descriptive argument for one ring model. It holds in the limit epsilon << J and Delta << 4J, and the value drops the Delta condition. Not a proved result.
theory_low.andriyash-frustrated-ring-suppression: Section IV B, p.7: an energetic argument for one example (violated-coupling counts). It needs J >> epsilon and is not proved. The sentence also ends with an authors' interpretation (topological obstructions, quantum advantage).
theory_low.andriyash-shamrock-exponential-advantage: Section IV C, p.7: the 2^K scaling is conditional on 'assuming all inter-path escape channels are topologically forbidden'. It is an argument supported by the numerical test (Fig. 6), not a proof.
theory_low.arute-2rdm-from-1rdm: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Eq. (4) and (A13) are the Wick factorization for a Slater determinant, cited to [29]. Appendix A restates it and does not derive it. The exactness-only-for-Slater caveat is quoted, but no proof is in the paper.
theory_low.arute-measurement-circuit-counts: Appendix C 3, p.15: 276, 149 and 13 are stated for N=12 without a derivation. 276 and 149 (the greedy grouping) are not shown. The text gives no theorem or proof, so it is not a proved result.
theory_low.arute-purification-convergence: Appendix E, pp.18-19: a moment-based recurrence under assumptions (mu_j <= alpha_j sigma^j, sigma small, Gaussian for the high-probability claim). The paper says its goal is 'to provide evidence' of convergence. An argument under assumptions, not a theorem with a proof.
theory_low.arute-purification-eigenvector-failure-p: Appendix E 2, p.20: a Chebyshev tail bound with assumptions (E <= 1/4, element variances). The quotes drop the conditions and the bound (E27) is only asymptotic (~). Not a stated theorem with full conditions.
theory_low.arute-hessian-optimizer-requirements: Appendix H, p.26: the claim that gradient and Hessian are computable from the 1-RDM is only stated, resting on the Slater 2-RDM identity (cited). Appendix H does not derive it. The concatenation step is method description. Not a proved result.
